_exec_summary.SummaryText:
The HB Fuller site is located on a 132.68-acre parcel of land near Simpsonville (Greenville County), South Carolina. HB Fuller produces acrylic polymers through water- based emulsion polymerization reactions. This process utilizes a number of chemicals as raw materials, two of which are listed as toxics under 40 CFR 68.130: acrylonitrile, and aqueous ammonia. Less than 2% of formaldehyde, is a residual reactant in a monomer, N-methylolacrylamide. 
One chemical, acrylonitrile is present in quantities above the threshold limits set forth for the RMP program. Furthermore, the process in which this chemical is used is subject to level 3 program requirements.

Acrylonitrile is handled and stored as a non-refrigerated liquid. Effects of acute exposure to high concentrations of acrylonitrile include irritation of the respiratory tract experienced as nasal discomfort and discharge, with chest pain, coughing, headache, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and drowsiness. At high doses acrylonitrile can be fatal by inhalation, ingestion, skin contact and other routes. The threshold quantity listed in 40 CFR 68.130 for acrylonitrile is 20,000 pounds. HB Fuller uses acrylonitrile as a raw material in an emulsion polymerization reaction and stores a quantity greater than the threshold amount in its monomer tank farm. HB Fuller has not had an accident or incident involving a reportable quantity of acrylonitrile over the last five years.

HB Fuller does not designate employees for response other than to address incidental releases of hazardous substances where the substance can be absorbed, neutralized, or otherwise controlled at the time of release by employees in the immediate release area, or by maintenance personnel, or by employees to clean-up a spill that does not pose an immediate safety or health hazard. These actions are not considered response under OSHA or Part 68; therefore, HB Fuller is a non-responding facility [40 CFR 68.90(b)]. For non-responding facilities, EPA has adopte

d a policy similar to OSHA in its Hazardous Waste Operations and Emergency Response (HAZWOPER) [29 CFR 1910.120].
This allows these facilities to develop an emergency action plan to ensure employee safety, rather than a full-fledged emergency response plan provided that they coordinate with local response agencies to ensure that they will be prepared to respond to an emergency at the facility.
HB Fuller operates in a manner that attempts to minimize hazards associated with the handling of chemicals. HB Fuller has several mechanisms in place for addressing a release of a regulated hazardous substance. These include the following:
a)	An Emergency Response Plan
b)	Written Safety Programs
c)	Written safe operating procedures, including one for unloading bulk railcars and tank trucks The Emergency Response Plan contains detailed information relating to materials stored on site, potential on-site emergencies, and action plans for handling on-site emergencies including accidental releases. Emergency contacts are identified and a notification procedure is detailed.
All production personnel are required to notify their immediate supervisor in the event of an identified emergency. The supervisor will then contact the plant Emergency Coordinator (EC). The Emergency Coordinator will contact the appropriate local response organizations and, as necessary, State and federal agencies. The Plan contains a call list designating these contacts.
In the event of severe weather, HB Fuller is dedicated to protecting its employees and the surrounding community. Procedures have been set up to warn plant employees and shut down key operations in order to minimize impact in the event of a weather related failure. The severe weather procedure is available for review at the site.
HB Fuller regularly receives shipments of acrylonitrile in tank trucks and transfers these materials into a dedicated above-ground storage tank located within the Monomer Tank Farm. The Monomer Tank Farm is complete wi

th secondary containment. Tank trucks are unloaded at a dedicated unloading station by trained personnel. HB Fuller has a documented procedure for these operators to follow. During delivery, the vapor in the headspace of these tanks is vented back to the delivering tanker. Normal breathing losses from the acrylonitrile and vinyl acetate storage tanks are vented through conservation vents to a thermal oxidizer.
HB Fuller controls the emissions of the odorous acrylate esters, vinyl acetate, and acrylonitrile with two thermal oxidizers operated interchangeably; usage is rotated between the two units. Breathing losses from the monomer storage tanks, emissions from the weigh tanks, and emissions from the reactors are collected in separate manifolds for treatment in the thermal oxidizer.
It is HB Fuller philosophy that all employees will be trained to perform their assigned duties safely as outlined in procedures. To this end, procedures were created to provide work instructions and training documentation tools for effectively and systematically planning training initiatives, assessing training needs, providing required employee training, and maintaining appropriate training records.

In order to ensure an efficient workplace, preventive maintenance is performed on a majority of the equipment at HB Fuller. These procedures are documented, and a copy of the related procedure is available for review at the site. 

HB Fuller has established a Management of Change procedure so that formulation, process, or equipment modifications and installations are reviewed prior to implementation to assure that safety issues are appropriately addressed, changes are communicated, and documentation is updated.

HB Fuller occasionally brings in outside contractors for specific tasks. Any contractor that is performing work in the manufacturing facility is given a safety briefing that includes:
a)	Emergency Evacuation Plan
b)	Site Safety Rules
c)	Location of Fire Extinguishers, Fire Exits, and

emergency Eye Wash/Shower Stations
d)	Location of and access to Safety Data Sheets
e)	Specific Hazards Workers May be Exposed To.
Further, a detailed review of the proper use of facility equipment and implementation of applicable Safety Programs (i.e., Hot Work, Confined Space, Lockout/Tagout, etc.) takes place as triggered.
